level1.text: An X-ray beam passes through a $6.8\,\text{cm}$ thick layer of soft tissue. The half-value thickness of soft tissue for this radiation is $3.4\,\text{cm}$. What percentage of the radiation gets through the tissue?

For a bone scan, a patient is given a technetium-$99\text{m}$ tracer with an activity of $600\,\text{MBq}$. The half-life of technetium-$99\text{m}$ is $6.01\,\text{h}$. How large is the activity of the tracer after $24.0\,\text{h}$, if nothing left the body? Give the answer in megabecquerels.

The effective dose of the FDG tracer of a PET scan is about $0.019\,\text{mSv}$ for an adult for every injected megabecquerel. How large an effective dose does the patient receive when injected with $300\,\text{MBq}$? Give the answer in millisieverts.

In radiotherapy, a tumour with a mass of $50\,\text{g}$ receives an absorbed dose of $2.0\,\text{Gy}$ in one treatment session. How much radiation energy does the tumour absorb during the session? Give the answer in joules.

A smoke detector contains americium-241 whose activity when new is $37\,\text{kBq}$. The half-life of americium-241 is $432\,\text{a}$. How large is the activity after $100\,\text{a}$? Give the answer in kilobecquerels.

level2.text: The activity of carbon-14 in the carbon of a living tree is measured to be $0.23\,\text{Bq}$ per gram. The corresponding activity of charcoal found at an archaeological dig is $0.029\,\text{Bq}$ per gram. The half-life of carbon-14 is $5700\,\text{a}$. How old is the charcoal? Give the answer in years to two significant figures.

In the thickness gauge of a steel mill, the $60\,\text{keV}$ gamma radiation of americium-241 passes through a thin steel strip to a detector. Without the strip the detector counts $1200$ photons per second and with the strip $900$ photons per second, once the background radiation has been subtracted. The half-value thickness of steel for this radiation is $0.73\,\text{mm}$. How thick is the strip? Give the answer in millimetres.

A patient receives an effective dose of $8.0\,\text{mSv}$ from a CT examination of the body. A person in Finland receives on average about $5.1\,\text{mSv}$ a year from natural radiation. How many days of natural radiation dose does the CT examination correspond to? A year has $365$ days.

Right after the tracer is injected, the dose rate of the radiation from a PET patient is $30\,\mu\text{Sv/h}$ at a distance of $1.0\,\text{m}$. A nurse helps the patient for $5.0\,\text{min}$ at a distance of $0.50\,\text{m}$. How large a dose does the nurse receive? Assume that the patient can be treated as a point source and that the dose rate stays constant during this time. Give the answer in microsieverts.

level3.text: A tumour receives $30$ radiotherapy sessions of $2.0\,\text{Gy}$ each. In each session the radiation is given from five different directions, and each beam gives the same share of the dose to the tumour. At the point where a beam enters, before the tumour, healthy tissue receives $1.3$ times the dose from the beam compared with what the same beam gives to the tumour. How large a total dose does healthy tissue at the entry point of one beam receive during the whole treatment? Assume that the other beams do not pass through this point. Give the answer in grays.

In mammography the voltage of the X-ray tube is about $30\,\text{kV}$, and the average energy of the photons is about $20\,\text{keV}$. Here assume that the energy of the photons is $30\,\text{keV}$. At this energy the half-value thickness of soft tissue is $1.8\,\text{cm}$ and that of bone or a calcification is $0.27\,\text{cm}$. Two beams of equal length pass through tissue: one through soft tissue alone, and in the other a $1.0\,\text{cm}$ stretch of soft tissue has been replaced by a calcified tissue of the same thickness that attenuates like bone. How many times greater is the intensity reaching the detector at the beam that passed through soft tissue alone?

For the $511\,\text{keV}$ photons of a PET tracer, the half-value thickness of lead is $3.9\,\text{mm}$. How thick a lead shield is needed around a syringe so that only $5.0\,\%$ of the radiation gets through the shield? Give the answer in millimetres.
